title: Alvise Mocenigo, Venetian ambassador at Rome, to Doge Lorenzo Priuli, 25 April 1558 (ASVe Busta 30 ff. 4-6, DECODE R1873)

steps.what: Fetched R1871-R1873 images with the DECODE cookie and viewed them; identified Alvise Mocenigo (Rome 25 Apr 1558, duplicate despatch to Doge Lorenzo Priuli) from the signature and clear text.
Grepped CSP Venice vi April 1558 on BHO for the Mocenigo despatch.
Followed Tomokiyo's R1872 note to Bonavoglia's page (live site HTTP 500); Wayback copy holds the R1873 transcription and full decipherment.

Split from the former combined target r1871 (catalogue 264) under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): R1873 (1558, letter+superscript nomenclator, Bonavoglia's decipherment) and R1871 (Foscarini 1680, three-digit code, not deciphered) are different ciphers 122 years apart. Folder, profile, page and ledgers separated; earlier steps are kept as recorded.

outcome.method_basis: The four cipher passages were taken from Paolo Bonavoglia's published transcription and decipherment on crittologia.eu (Wayback copy); nothing was deciphered here and the key was not rebuilt.
outcome.notes: Bonavoglia's decipherment covers all four passages (176 signs); not re-checked sign by sign here. Nothing about the text is added.

credits.note: "Decifra dispacci veneziani" (crittologia.eu): transcription and full decipherment of R1873
note on DECODE R1872 pointing to Bonavoglia's decipherments

prior.where: crittologia.eu/critto/venezia_nomenclatore.html (Bonavoglia); pointer in Tomokiyo's note on DECODE R1872

human: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
